title: Naturality of the evaluation-defined closed adjunction comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], each equipped with a tensor bifunctor $\otimes$ (it assigns an object $X\otimes Y$ to each pair of objects and a morphism $f\otimes g$ to each pair of morphisms, preserving identities and componentwise composition); no associator, unitor, symmetry or coherence condition is assumed. In each of them let $H(X,Y)$ be a bifunctor, contravariant in $X$ and covariant in $Y$, with bijections $\Theta_{T,X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes X,Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(X,Y))$ natural in all three variables: $\Theta(g\circ k\circ(t\otimes a))=H(a,g)\circ\Theta(k)\circ t$ for $k:T\otimes X	o Y$, $t:T'	o T$, $a:X'	o X$ and $g:Y	o Y'$. Write $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}=\Theta^{-1}(1_{H(X,Y)}):H(X,Y)\otimes X	o Y$ for evaluation; call $\Theta(k)$ the tensor-Hom transpose of $k$. Let $F:\mathcal C	o\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D	o\mathcal C$ be functors, let $\mu_{X,Y}:FX\otimes FY\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X\otimes Y)$ be isomorphisms natural in $X,Y$, that is $F(f\otimes g)\circ\mu_{X,Y}=\mu_{X',Y'}\circ(Ff\otimes Fg)$, and let $F\dashv G$ be an adjunction with unit $u$ and counit $e$ and the natural Hom-bijection convention of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. For $P\in\mathcal C$ and $N\in\mathcal D$, define $b_{P,N}:F H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)	o H_{\mathcal D}(FP,N)$ to be the tensor-Hom transpose of
$$F H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)\otimes FP\xrightarrow{\mu}F(H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)\otimes P)\xrightarrow{F(\mathrm{ev})}FGN\xrightarrow{e_N}N.$$
Put $\delta_{P,N}=G(b_{P,N})\circ u_{H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)}$. For every $a:P'	o P$ in $\mathcal C$ and $v:N	o N'$ in $\mathcal D$, these specified maps satisfy
$$b_{P',N'}\circ F H_{\mathcal C}(a,Gv)=H_{\mathcal D}(Fa,v)\circ b_{P,N},$$
$$\delta_{P',N'}\circ H_{\mathcal C}(a,Gv)=G H_{\mathcal D}(Fa,v)\circ\delta_{P,N}.$$
Thus $b$ and its adjoint $\delta$ are natural in both variables for these evaluation-defined choices; no invertibility assertion is part of this statement. In particular the statement applies when $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ are monoidal and $(F,\mu)$ is strong monoidal, but only the tensor bifunctors and the naturality of $\mu$ enter.

proof.text: For either category, naturality of $\Theta$ in $T$, applied to $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}$ and $t=z:T\to H(X,Y)$, gives $\Theta(\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}\circ(z\otimes1_X))=z$, since $\Theta(\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y})=1$. Thus $\Theta^{-1}(z)=\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}\circ(z\otimes1_X)$. In particular equality of maps into $H(X,Y)$ can be checked after this uncurrying. This uses only the assumed bijectivity and naturality, and the identity laws of [def-nagata-category].

proof.text: For $a:X\prime\to X$ and $g:Y\to Y\prime$, apply $\Theta_{H(X,Y),X\prime,Y\prime}$ to the two maps $\mathrm{ev}_{X\prime,Y\prime}\circ(H(a,g)\otimes1_{X\prime})$ and $g\circ\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}\circ(1_{H(X,Y)}\otimes a)$. The first has transpose $H(a,g)$ by step 1; the second has transpose $H(a,g)\circ1\circ1=H(a,g)$ by the assumed three-variable naturality. Injectivity proves the evaluation identity between these two maps. All objects and arrows here are in the single category being considered; no symmetry or reassociation of tensor factors is used. The simplifications are the identity laws of [def-nagata-category].

proof.text:
Put $A=H_{\mathcal C}(P,GN)$, $A\prime=H_{\mathcal C}(P\prime,GN\prime)$ and $h=H_{\mathcal C}(a,Gv):A\to A\prime$. Let $k_{P,N}=e_N\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ\mu_{A,P}$, so that $b_{P,N}=\Theta_{\mathcal D}(k_{P,N})$. Naturality of $\mu$ at $(h,1_{P\prime})$, step 2 in $\mathcal C$, and then naturality of the counit give, in order,
$$\begin{aligned}k_{P\prime,N\prime}\circ(Fh\otimes1_{FP\prime})&=e_{N\prime}\circ F\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{P\prime,GN\prime}\circ(h\otimes1_{P\prime})\bigr)\circ\mu_{A,P\prime}\\&=e_{N\prime}\circ FGv\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ F(1_A\otimes a)\circ\mu_{A,P\prime}\\&=v\circ e_N\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_{P,GN})\circ\mu_{A,P}\circ(1_{FA}\otimes Fa)\\&=v\circ k_{P,N}\circ(1_{FA}\otimes Fa).\end{aligned}$$
The third equality also uses naturality of $\mu$ at $(1_A,a)$. The counit equation $e_{N\prime}\circ FGv=v\circ e_N$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]; associativity is [def-nagata-category]. Both sides have source $FA\otimes FP\prime$ and target $N\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), adjunction maps and formulas immediately following the definition. Agent-written tensor-Hom consequence using the natural bijections explicitly assumed in the statement.

proof.text: Apply the assumed bijection $\Theta^{\mathcal D}_{FA,FP\prime,N\prime}$ to step 3. Naturality in the first variable $T$ gives transpose $b_{P\prime,N\prime}\circ Fh$ on the left. Naturality in $X$ and $Y$ gives transpose $H_{\mathcal D}(Fa,v)\circ b_{P,N}$ on the right. This is exactly the asserted equation for $b$. These are direct substitutions into the stated naturality formula; identity compositions are simplified using [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), adjunction maps and formulas immediately following the definition. Agent-written tensor-Hom consequence using the natural bijections explicitly assumed in the statement.

proof.text:
Write $q=H_{\mathcal D}(Fa,v)$ and use the defining formula for $\delta$. Naturality of the unit from [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], evaluated at $h:A\to A\prime$, says $u_{A\prime}\circ h=GFh\circ u_A$. Therefore, by step 4 and functoriality of $G$,
$$\delta_{P\prime,N\prime}\circ h=Gb_{P\prime,N\prime}\circ GFh\circ u_A=G(b_{P\prime,N\prime}\circ Fh)\circ u_A=G(q\circ b_{P,N})\circ u_A=Gq\circ\delta_{P,N}.$$
Associativity is [def-nagata-category]. The adjunction formula $\Psi(b)=Gb\circ u$ in the cited statement also confirms that this specified $\delta$ is the adjoint of $b$. This proves both naturality clauses for arbitrary $a,v$; no comparison map or counit was inverted.
